The AI caricature trend. In roughly eight days, we saw: - a one-line prompt - harden into a template - replicate at scale - generate its own discourse - and then quietly become a product feature Now the act of making becomes the act of selecting. As LLM product features evolve, perhaps the most interesting part isn’t what it can generate. It’s what it quietly trains us not to do anymore. ...more

For the last three years, Robin Jones and I have been talking AI together. Unsurprisingly, there’s one topic that never goes away: - What does the future of our day-to-day work look like? - What happens to *actual* human agency in an increasingly agentic professional environment? - And what (if anything) can we do to shape this? On March 10th, we’ll be sharing some of those hopes, fears and ambitions on stage at PharmaBrands second London Age of AI event. Will we have any definitive answers? No. Will we have managed to process the impacts of the latest crop of benchmark-slaying models by then? Possibly. Will it be more useful than helplessly doom-scrolling predictions of a white-collar apocalypse here on LinkedIn? Definitely. Also far more fun. Tickets available here: https://lnkd.in/esDzetaP ...more ...more

I'm running on empty this year, so I'm not doing what I've done the last three Christmases - opening up my diary, rallying donations to the Trussell Trust, trying to build a little wave of collective generosity. I don't have it in me But I've still made the donation, because whatever Christmas means, it has to mean something about showing up for each other when things are hard. And things are very, very hard for a lot of people right now If you're able to give anything this Christmas, here's where it could go FOOD Nearly 1/4 of working parents in the UK used a food support service in the past year. That's 1.7m people who are going to work and still can't feed their families. 1-in-4 of them are visiting a food bank every 2 weeks Over 3m emergency food parcels were distributed by the Trussell Trust last year - 1m of those to children. That number is climbing. These food banks are stretched to breaking point, trying to catch people our society has let fall If you can help: https://lnkd.in/e8EP5iHn Or search for your local food bank/drop off points TOYS I've given to a few toy drives because so many parents are making impossible calculations - Dinner or presents. Heating or a tree. The humiliation of not being able to give your child even one small thing to unwrap A charity in Scotland posted that they'd had to send volunteers home because there were not enough toy donations to package up. I know many are feeling the pinch, but even something for a few pounds could mean everything to a child on Christmas morning I keep thinking about little ones padding downstairs, hoping, and finding nothing. Believing that Santa looked at their house and decided they weren't worth visiting. That breaks something in me If you can help: https://lnkd.in/ea4PqtNa https://lnkd.in/e6f-c5Cq https://lnkd.in/ewY-Rsat GAZA And then there's what keeps me up at night Right now, Palestinian families are trying to survive another day in freezing, flooded tents while winter winds tear at the fabric. Several babies have frozen to death in the last week, winter has barely begun. There is mass starvation. Almost no medical care. Aid is being blocked. There is no ceasefire. And we keep scrolling past their trauma like it's just content These are parents trying to keep their children alive, watching the world look away. If you do one thing this Christmas, please consider supporting the people working on the ground: https://lnkd.in/eQkaejFx https://hopeandplay.org/ https://lnkd.in/gi8AXizk Maybe this reads as virtue signalling, honestly I don't care if it does I'm just hoping it reaches a few people who have something to spare - money, attention, anything - and that it makes one family's Christmas slightly less brutal than it would have been That's all any of us can do And it matters ...more ...more

For me, the most useful AI conversations start with a simple question: how could we do this differently? I really enjoyed spending a full day in London with commercial colleagues, exploring how an AI+ mindset can help us rethink real-life workflows and accelerate delivery. We got hands-on with emerging agentic AI capabilities, exploring how new technologies and models could support practical business needs. Rather than adding AI at the end of an existing process, we worked together to examine workflows, identify opportunities, and prioritise the ideas with the greatest potential. What stood out most was the value of working through these questions together. Different perspectives helped us challenge assumptions, focus on the right problems, and move from exploration to practical next steps. Thank you to my great teammates for joining, contributing so openly, and bringing so many thoughtful perspectives to the discussion! And a big thank you to Lucrezia Noli , Soma Ray , Mark Goff and Sandeep Khanna for hosting us at the innovation centre and bringing new developments in agentic AI to life in such a practical and engaging way. #AI #AIPlus #AgenticAI #Innovation #Collaboration #BusinessTransformation #FutureOfWork

18 months ago, I started a complete career pivot with my one-month-old son in my arms. Leaving a successful career in pharmaceutical marketing to step into the world of prime London real estate felt equal parts exciting and daunting. There were moments when it genuinely felt like a leap into the unknown. Has this been one of the most challenging periods of my career? Absolutely. Has it also been one of the most rewarding? Without question. I've learned more than expected. I've been stretched in ways I couldn't have predicted. And more than once, I've surprised myself with what was possible on the other side of uncertainty. What began as a company rebrand wasn't just a change of industry, it was a change of perspective. Today, I'm fortunate to be surrounded by exceptional colleagues, building meaningful campaigns, creating standout content, and helping shape the growth of a business in one of the most dynamic property markets in the world: London. The biggest surprise? The leap of faith that felt so risky at the time doesn't feel like a leap anymore. It feels like exactly where I was supposed to land. For now, I'm staying put, enjoying the journey, and looking forward to what we build next.
